pr_title: Add WT_SESSION to WSLENV so it propagates into WSL
pr_body:
This makes sure that things running inside WSL can see `WT_SESSION`.

Closes #3948.
pr_comments: I moved the environment block load to before we set the variables because we need to read WSLENV. I had to replace WT_SESSION with `insert_or_assign` because `emplace` _does not overwrite_.

issue_context.title: WT_SESSION doesn’t appear in WSL
issue_context.body:
We did not realize that `WT_SESSION` wouldn’t appear in WSL because it’s not in `WSLENV`.

This may also impact VS Code.

/cc @mixmastamyk
comments: @benhillis is it valid for us as a hosting application to prepend to the user’s `WSLENV`?

:tada:This issue was addressed in #4157, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v0.8.10091.0`.:tada:

review_comments: You only need to prepend the key and not also the value? Is `WSLENV` then just a list of keys that WSL should copy from the environment block? That's not totally clear without thinking about it/outside reference so perhaps add that as a comment here.
